newsitem.title: USA: Senate panel approves U.S. intelligence funds.
newsitem.headline: Senate panel approves U.S. intelligence funds.

text.p: The Senate Intelligence Committee said Thursday it had approved behind closed doors the bill authorising funding for intelligence activities next year.

The panel approved the bill Wednesday in a closed session. The House Intelligence Committee was expected to take it up Thursday. The bill authorises spending for the Central Intelligence Agency and other intelligence activities.
Although many of those activities remain secret, the bill does call for a better process of getting information out to families like those of Marine guards killed in an attack in El Salvador in 1985.

If that policy had been in place then the families would not have had to "wait 12 years to learn of the circumstances surrounding this tragic event," Senate Intelligence Committee Chairman Richard Shelby, an Alabama Republican, said in a statement.
The bill also clarifies that federal employees can inform the proper congressional authorities of wrongdoing without fear of reprisal, even if the evidence involves classified information.

Misunderstandings about that policy "undermines Congress' ability to fulfil its constitutional responsiblity and is particularly troubling when intelligence agencies are involved," said the panel's senior Democrat, Sen. Bob Kerrey of Nebraska.
